$comment: What a KEY makes certain, and nothing else. A `case:` holds an expression and a `goto:` names a destination because of the key beside them — no schema knowledge needed, so this is safe wherever a definition is read. Whether any OTHER scalar computes depends on its slot, which only the server knows: internal/lsp/semantic.go answers that as semantic tokens.

routing.$comment: A goto/switch target, sigil included: nothing styles `punctuation.definition.keyword`, so capturing the `$` apart from the name left it uncoloured beside a coloured name. Restricted to a scalar that is nothing but `$name`, so a stray `$word` inside a URL stays the literal text the parser makes it. Scoped as a function name because that is what themes colour.

string-escape.$comment: YAML's own escape rule does not reach inside this region, and without this the `"` of a `\"` reads as the end of the enclosing scalar.
string-escape.name: constant.character.escape.yaml

root.$comment: The context roots evalEnv builds (internal/engine/evaluator.go); `last_error` precedes `error` so the longer name wins. It carries the SAME scope as the segments after it — a path is one referent, and `variable.language` is a different colour from `variable.other.property` in most themes.
root.name: variable.other.genroc

object-key.$comment: Included only from #braces: elsewhere a bare word before a colon is not a key.
object-key.name: variable.other.genroc

case-double.$comment: A `case` is the one expression written BARE (internal/lsp/CLAUDE.md), so it is found through its own key — by LOOKING BEHIND at it, never consuming it: an injection that takes over a key gives it a different stack from every other key in the file.
case-double.name: meta.embedded.expression.genroc

case-single.$comment: A `case` is the one expression written BARE (internal/lsp/CLAUDE.md), so it is found through its own key — by LOOKING BEHIND at it, never consuming it: an injection that takes over a key gives it a different stack from every other key in the file.
case-single.name: meta.embedded.expression.genroc

routing-keyword.$comment: `end` and `next` are the rest of the destination vocabulary — a routing slot is every task plus these two — so they carry the SAME scope as `$name`. Scoping them as a keyword put two colours in one slot (#FF7B72 against #D2A8FF in Dark 2026). Matched through their key so an ordinary string reading "end" is left alone. Read behind the key rather than through it, so the key stays YAML's.

routing-keyword-quoted.$comment: The same target written inside quotes, matched from within the string so YAML keeps it.
